## Pull Request

### Description
What does this PR do? Provide a brief summary of the changes.

### Type of Change
- [ ] Feature (new functionality)
- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes)
- [ ] Dependency update
- [ ] CI/CD changes

### Related Issue
Closes #(issue number)

Related to: #(issue numbers, if any)

### Testing
How was this tested? Describe the test scenarios.

- [ ] Unit tests pass
- [ ] Integration tests pass
- [ ] Manual testing completed

**Test coverage:** _X%_

### Documentation
- [ ] README updated (if needed)
- [ ] API documentation updated (if needed)
- [ ] Comments added to complex code
- [ ] Module manifest updated (if needed)
- [ ] docs/ folder updated (if needed)

### Screenshots / Logs
(If applicable: UI changes, error messages, performance metrics, etc.)

```
Paste logs or error messages here
```

### Checklist
- [ ] Code follows project style guide (see CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [ ] Commits are logically organized
- [ ] Commit messages follow Conventional Commits format
- [ ] No breaking changes (or clearly documented)
- [ ] Tests written for new functionality
- [ ] All tests passing locally
- [ ] No debugging code or console.logs left
- [ ] No secrets or credentials in code
- [ ] Linked to related issue

### Risk Assessment
What could go wrong with this change?

- [ ] Low risk (isolated change)
- [ ] Medium risk (affects existing functionality)
- [ ] High risk (breaking change, touches core logic)

**Risk mitigation:** Describe how risks are mitigated.

### Notes for Reviewers
Any additional context or areas to focus on?

---

**Before submitting:**
1. Ensure all checks pass
2. Self-review your code
3. Fill out all sections
4. Link the issue
